newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Ruling party edges left in final El Salvador vote.
newsitem.headline: Ruling party edges left in final El Salvador vote.

text.p: El Salvador's right-wing ruling party edged leftist former guerrillas by a slight margin in the Central American country's March 18 election, final results released on Tuesday showed.

The Republican National Alliance, known as ARENA, won 28 seats in the 84-member Legislative Assembly to 27 for the Farabundo Marti National Liberation Front (FMLN), the Supreme Electoral Tribunal (TSE) said.

But the FMLN nonetheless posted significant gains, trailing ARENA in Congress by 39 to 21 before the election, and solidified the party as a major electoral force after a disappointing electoral debut in 1994.
It was the country's second election since the end of El Salvador's 12-year civil war, which killed an estimated 75,000 people. The first was in 1994.

The remainder of the seats on the Legislative Assembly were split among several parties, with the conservative National Conciliation Party taking 11 and the Christian Democrats 10. Eight seats went to four parties.
ARENA fared much better in the races for 262 mayoral posts, winning 161 compared to 53 for the FMLN. But the FMLN took the largest municipal prize, the capital of San Salvador.
